label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. If a cookie banner offers no way to decline that works, accept it, report that as a problem, and carry on. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

outcome.reason: The shop refused every Add to cart with an error that asks to close the tab or disable extensions, on several products: that is how bot protection treats an automated browser. Not counted as an accessibility result.

reclassified.why: The shop refused every Add to cart with an error that asks to close the tab or disable extensions, on several products: that is how bot protection treats an automated browser.

findings.problem: After pressing Deny Cookies, keyboard focus landed on an unlabeled [name] Policy div instead of moving to a sensible place, so I was unsure the choice had worked.

Before reaching the main menu I had to tab through about ten repeated links all named Shop now, plus carousel buttons with no name, with no way to tell them apart. It took roughly 15 key presses to reach GIFTS/NEW/[name].
[name] arrow and other icon buttons have no accessible name, only an icon, so I could not tell what they do.
The Skip to Main Content link only moved focus to the breadcrumb Home link, not to the products. I still had to tab through filters and about 3 unnamed icon buttons to reach the first product.

The product has no clear link with its name. The first focusable item is a link with no name, and a button called 2025 [name]™ Fair Isle sweater undefined that did nothing when pressed (broken label, raw HTML entity and the word undefined). Only the nameless link opened the product.

Out-of-stock sizes are focusable, so I had to tab through six sold-out sizes before reaching the first available one. Focus then looped from the size chart back to the first size, and Add to Bag could not be reached until I pressed Escape to close the size list. This was not explained anywhere.

Pressing Add to Bag showed only ADDING, then focus was lost to the top of the page. The error We are sorry, this item cannot be added to your bag appeared only as plain text with no focus or announcement, so I had to re-read the page to find out. I could not continue to checkout and did not reach the payment step.
